h1: Dener fiber lasers — GFL production lasers and the Smart series, 5 × 10 to 13 × 82 ft, 3 to 40 kW
intro: Dener's sheet lasers are the premium line of NovoTech's laser section: built in Kayseri, Turkey, on stress-relieved frames with IPG, Raycus or nLIGHT sources, Precitec autofocus heads and nesting software, and backed by Dener Canada parts in Mississauga. The GFL is the production machine — a space-frame gantry rated for 1.5 G and 394 ft/min, a pallet changer that loads the next sheet while the first is cut, in 5 × 10, 6.6 × 13 and 6.6 × 20 ft with 3 to 40 kW. The Smart series comes from the same factory at a lower price: the closed-type with laser-safe cabin and double exchange table in six sizes to a 41 ft bed, the semi-closed single-table machines from 8.2 × 20 to 13 × 82 ft for long plate, and the open-type 3 – 6 kW entry laser. Loading towers, sheet storage, bevel heads and air-cutting packages are available for all of them. A 6 kW machine cuts 3/4″ mild steel; 12 kW cuts 1″, 20 – 40 kW 1-1/2″ and beyond. Installed, trained and supported from Mississauga, ON.

faq.q: GFL or Smart — what is the difference?
faq.a: Both come from Dener's Kayseri plant with the same sources, heads and software. The GFL is the production machine: a heavier stress-relieved frame and space-frame bridge rated for 1.5 G, a pallet changer and the full option list — the machine for two shifts a day. The Smart series is built to a lower price: the closed-type still has a double exchange table and 1 G, the semi-closed machines offer very large single tables, and the open-type is the entry-level 3 – 6 kW laser. Same cut quality; the GFL is faster between parts and lasts longer at high duty.

faq.q: Which Smart — closed, semi-closed or open?
faq.a: Closed-type when you cut all day: the double exchange table keeps the laser cutting while you load, and the cabin keeps fumes and the beam inside. Semi-closed when the parts are long — 20 to 82 ft single tables for beams, ship sections and plate that no standard laser takes. Open-type when the budget comes first and the sheets are loaded by hand or forklift from any side: 3 or 6 kW, 5 × 10 to 6.6 × 20 ft, the lowest-priced Dener laser.

faq.q: What is in a Dener laser as standard?
faq.a: An IPG, Raycus or nLIGHT fiber source, a Precitec or Raytools autofocus cutting head with capacitive height sensing and collision protection, a stress-relieved welded frame, pneumatic fume-extraction compartments under the table and scrap boxes on wheels, a chiller, a CNC with nesting software, cutting database and production reports, and a remote handset. Cutting gas regulators, dust collector connections and the CSA-approved panel with a 600 V transformer are included in the NovoTech package.

A loading / unloading tower that feeds the pallet changer, sheet storage with several shelves for lights-out production, part sorting, a bevel head for weld preparation, a marking head, and the intelligent air-cutting package that replaces nitrogen on sheet to about 1/4″. The GFL and the closed-type Smart are prepared for the tower from the factory.

faq.q: How does Dener compare with the Senfeng value line?
faq.a: Dener is the premium line — heavier frame rated for 1.5 G, Precitec heads, IPG / nLIGHT sources, longer life at high duty and Dener Canada parts in Mississauga. Senfeng builds its own sources and heads and sells for less, with a range Dener does not cover (4 × 4 ft compact machines, 60 kW plate gantries, sheet-and-tube combos, coil-fed lines). The comparison, the laser power guide and the capacity table for both lines are on the sheet laser cutters overview.

faq.q: What does the machine need on site?
faq.a: A level floor, 600 V 3-phase (with the transformer we supply) or 480 V, a chiller (included), assist gas — oxygen for mild steel, nitrogen or compressed air for stainless and aluminum — a dust collector and a compressed-air supply. A 6 kW GFL 3015 draws about 30 kW in total and needs roughly 33 × 20 ft with the pallet changer. Delivery, installation and operator training are done by NovoTech from Mississauga.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models with a small enough motor. Manual machines have no electrics.
